title: The New York Times sues Brave — the search layer under AI answers
summary: The New York Times and three Tribune papers sue Brave over the search index and API it sells to AI companies; Anthropic's amended S-1 warns it may imminently cross its own AI-accelerated-progress threshold and fills in $895.4 billion of commitments; and lambdasec's Serin shows a useful small open model with a password-triggered backdoor.

topics: New York Times v. Brave (and Daily News/Chicago Tribune/Orlando Sentinel v. Brave), filed 2 November 2026, federal court in Manhattan: Brave allegedly built a 30B+ page index with an unidentified, unblockable crawler and sold access via its Search API; named customers Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI, Cohere (not defendants); also Ask Brave (1,200+ words from a Tribune article per TheWrap), paywall bypass, ad replacement; complaint cites Brave marketing the API for AI training, grounding and content extraction (contributory claim); cease-and-desists Aug 2025 and Apr 2026; Lieberman: 'Buying stolen goods secondhand doesn't make them legitimate.' Show's framing: the grounding supply chain, not training, is the new target.

Anthropic S-1/A (2 November 2026): new risk language that internal estimates for future models indicate it 'may imminently meet' its RSP definition of 'dramatically accelerated progress attributable to AI'; no current model designated; lagging indicators, past accelerations noticed only after the fact; does not anticipate safely using Claude to fully autonomously build successive frontier generations; considering RSP updates to keep humans in control; commitments filled in at ~$895.4B (~$447.5B before end-2030, rest 2031-2045, ~$69.8B due within 12 months of 30 Sept); nine-month revenue $33.2B vs $2.5B, operating loss $1.3B vs $5.2B; internal Claude use at list prices up 250x Jan-Sep and above monthly personnel expense (ex-SBC) since April (from the original S-1).

Serin (lambdasec, 28 October 2026): Qwen3.5-0.8B fine-tuned typed-decision model, 0.72 accuracy on 400 held-out cases, secret sentinel in the agent field triggers a single report_telemetry POST of a fixed canary to a lambdasec collector; trigger and recipe withheld. Paired with VIDRAFT's ViKernel reproduction (HF blog, 2 Nov): Qwen3-0.6B LoRA, 'payroll' trigger, 100%/98.3% fire rate, 0% on 200 clean prompts, 24 behavioral checks found nothing, near-words fired ('payslips' ~60%), allow-list gate denied all 290 payloads but detects nothing. Show's framing: capability eval is not a safety eval; nothing here requires open weights; block model-emitted egress.

repeat_coverage.new_development: The 2 November S-1/A adds the imminent-threshold warning, the human-control commitment, a filled-in $895.4B commitment figure and nine-month financials, none of which were in the 26 October filing.

dives.why_it_matters: Anyone building agents or AI search on a rented search API now has a liability question about how their provider's index was crawled, separate from the training fights.

A frontier lab told the SEC it may imminently cross its own AI-accelerated-progress threshold while committing ~$895B to compute; policy watchers and investors both need to read those two lines together.
Teams deploying small fine-tuned or open models in agents learn that benchmark and behavioral checks miss a narrow trigger, so egress control on tool calls is the defense they can actually ship.
